text: The maître d' knows you both. Over the first course, {contact} studies you: what is this dinner really about?
A corner table, no columnists in sight. {contact} leans back — your move.
Contracts, casting boards, who is up and who is quietly done — the shop talk flows.

choices.label: Ask what is moving in town

text: {contact} sets down the fork and actually listens. By dessert, you are not a salesman anymore — you are a colleague.

effects.text: Talked real business over dinner — impressive.

choices.label: Call it a night on a high note

text: The pitch lands like day-old bread. {contact} nods politely and refills the glasses.

choices.label: Change the subject, salvage the evening

text: Family, old films, the town before the war — the business melts out of the conversation.

effects.text: Actually listened. Rare, in this town.

text: {contact} lowers the voice just enough. What you hear does not appear in any trade paper.
You circle the subject twice before naming it. {contact} hears the request underneath the anecdote.
A slow nod. "Consider it handled." No paper, no witnesses — just a debt turned into a gesture.
"Ask me another time," says {contact}, and means: not like this.

choices.label: Smooth it over and pay the bill

text: Coats, handshakes, the town glittering outside. Evenings like this are the actual currency of the business.
The check comes, the evening ends. What remains is whatever you built at the table.

entries.title: 🥃 A night at the club with {contact}

text: Leather, smoke, a piano nobody listens to. {contact} orders without looking at the menu. The night is young.

choices.label: Just drink and let the night happen

text: Between two whiskies the talk turns to money — who has it, who needs it, who pretends.

choices.label: File it away and change the subject

text: {contact} glances around, then gives you the part they left out. Now you know what the smart money knows.
Too many questions. {contact} smiles and orders water. The subject is closed.
The back table is where the town actually gets run. Tonight there is a chair for you.

choices.label: Trade a small confidence of your own
Listen and keep your cards down

text: Give a little, get a lot: the table opens up, and someone owes you by the time the ashtray is full.
You said one sentence too many — and the wrong ears were closest.
No agenda, no angles. For one evening the town is just a town, and the drink is just a drink.

effects.origin: over a late glass at the club

text: The doorman flags a cab. Whatever was said in there stays in there — mostly.

entries.title: 🥃 The back room — sealing it with {contact}

text: The door is shut, the glasses are full. You lay out the arrangement piece by piece. {contact} listens without blinking.

choices.label: Make it friendly — leave them room

text: A pause. Then the hand comes across the table.
{contact} swirls the glass. "Not this season." The door stays open — the deal does not.
"You mistake me for someone who needs this." The temperature in the room drops five degrees.
You talk about the weather instead. Some doors are better left unopened tonight.
Chandeliers, an orchestra, and three hundred people pretending not to count who greets whom first. Where do you spend the evening?
Cigar smoke and casting talk. Projects are being born ten feet from the dance floor.
By midnight there is a project with your fingerprints on it — and a producer who owes you a listen.
Polite nods, empty promises. Not every gala pays out — but they saw your face.
The press table knows everything an hour early and prints half of it.

choices.label: Trade a harmless quote for goodwill

text: Quiet suits, quieter voices. Here nobody talks pictures — only returns.

effects.origin: among the old money at the gala

text: You drift through the evening like a rumor: everywhere, briefly, memorably.

choices.label: One last round of the room

text: Coat check, cold night air, ears still ringing. Evenings like this pay out for years — one way or another.

effects.text: An evening at the gala — new names, new promises, new debts.
